newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DUNCAN TASTES GLORY SECOND TIME ROUND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUNCAN TASTES GLORY SECOND TIME ROUND.

text.p: In a distinguished career as a striker with Tottenham and Derby, Scotsman John Duncan never reached an English F.A. Cup final.
In fact, he never even got as far as the quarter-finals and probably didn't think that would change when he took over as manager of perennial strugglers Chesterfield in 1993.
Formed in 1866, the fourth-oldest league club in England reached the fifth round three times, the last time back in 1950, but hardly had a Cup tradition.

That was until Saturday when they not only beat, but completely outplayed premier league Nottingham Forest to reach the quarter-finals for the first time in their long and pretty undistinguished history.
Duncan has built a team with the best defence in the league -- only 20 goals conceded in 28 games -- but no-one could have expected that to be enough to overcome Forest.

As it turned out, his well-drilled defence had a far easier day than they could have ever hoped for as toothless Forest -- crucially missing suspended player-manager Stuart Pearce -- limped out of the competition with barely a whimper.
"We pride ourselves on our defence but outplayed them all over the park," a delirious Duncan said after Saturday's famous win.
"It was a great team performance and I'm absolutely delighted."
Nearly 9,000 fans crammed into the old Saltergate ground to witness the giant-killing and loved every minute of it.
"We've made history," Duncan said. "It's brilliant for the town and the players are an absolute credit. We fully deserved to win the game."
The only goal came in the 54th minute when Tom Curtis sent his penalty past stand-in goalkeeper Alan Fettis.
Fettis had come on after Mark Crossley had been red-carded for bringing down Jon Howard as the forward bore down on goal.
But this was no backs-to-the-wall fluke upset. The team pushing for promotion from the second division were on top long before the sending-off and in total control afterwards.
Howard will have nightmares about one miss five minutes from time when he completely fluffed his shot after rounding Fettis and having only an empty goal to hit.
But the memory of that miss will fade while the victory will live on.
Goalscorer Curtis said he was "slightly nervous" about taking the penalty but just "hit it as hard and low as I could".
But while everyone in the town of Chesterfield celebrates, the fans of Forest will despair.
Since Pearce took over the manager's job the team have hauled themselves out of the relegation zone and were hoping for a good cup run to boost confidence. This is hardly what they had in mind.
"We were well and truly beaten by a team that had more endeavour, more organisation and fully deserved to beat us," Pearce said.
"It was the manner of the defeat that concerns me. Maybe some of the players think they're better than they are."
So Forest return to the battle for premier league survival and Chesterfield can dream of Wembley -- but not yet.
"We've got an important game against Rotherham on Tuesday," said Duncan before joining his players in full voice in the changing-rooms.
